Article Title: Students protest: Breakthrough with Sonam Wangchuk may help government tackle crisis
Article Text:
Sonam Wangchuk when he broke his hunger strike

NEW DELHI: Government is keeping its fingers crossed after its successful attempt to persuade activist Sonam Wangchuk - whose wide recognition helped expand the reach of Cockroach Janta Party's protest into uncomfortable territory for BJP - to break his hunger strike.CJP's assertion, though, to continue and even escalate the agitation if its demand for education minister Dharmendra Pradhan 's resignation is not met has muddied the waters, but govt feels the successful engagement with the Ladakh activist coupled with measures taken by it will help counter the allegation that govt has not been sensitive to students' concerns and resonate with those not affiliated with AAP, the Left and other opponents and their student outfits.The breakthrough with Wangchuk became possible because of deft footwork, including behind-the-scenes moves by home minister Amit Shah, that saw ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh overcoming the activist and bringing in local netas of Ladakh. Wangchuk's fears about violence and the risk of protests being overtaken - something that he articulated in the video-graphed conversation with the ministers - were helpful.Official circles are hopeful that Wangchuk's appeal for peaceful protests and against any form of violence, besides govt's positive response to his demand for not registering criminal cases against peaceful protestors and suitable compensation to families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide, will have a positive impact and may also help isolate "genuine" students from activists motivated by a dizzying array of motives - from partisan political considerations and gender fluidity to angst over Brahmanical patriarchy and Manuvad and Hindutva dominance.Unlike Abhijeet Dipke-led CJP, Wangchuk has not insisted on Pradhan's resignation. Considering it as the hook that connected that segment of youth with the protest who are not overtly political and might have been even otherwise sympathetic to some of the causes of the party, Wangchuk nuancing his pitch for accountability for paper leaks and expanding it beyond the individual to the ministry should help a govt pitted against a determined and competitive push for the minister's scalp.PM Modi was quick on X to wish the Ladakh activist - who was detained under NSA last year for his alleged role in violent protest in the UT - and that he regains the weight he lost in the fast.CJP could not have been pleased with the turn of events, but it was careful not to express its annoyance. Dipke lauded Wangchuk's "extraordinary courage" but left no doubt that he would carry on with his protest until Pradhan was sacked.The rift was evident after Wangchuk's wife Gitanjali Angmo wrote on X, "Before you rush to criticise Wangchuk, first pause to earn the ethos of fasting for 26 days for a cause larger than yourself. He lies in the ICU today, having lost 11 kg, including muscle mass, because he chose sacrifice over comfort... The least we can offer him is a day of compassion before burdening him with our own expectations and political calculations. Not everyone is qualified to judge a life of selfless service. One must first earn the moral stature to do so. Please. Have a heart."Also read: CJP-Centre 3rd round of talks today; PM Modi, Wangchuk release late night video - top developments BJP's Amit Malviya was quick to take a jibe at Dipke, saying there is now little justification for "his gang" to continue the protest and alleged their objective no longer appears to address students' concerns but to manufacture a political victory by insisting on Pradhan's resignation. It was Wangchuk's forcible removal, although with court authorisation from the protest site on July 18 that imparted the first real burst of agitational energy into the campaign, before the protestors' march to Parliament and police's alleged heavy-handedness turned it into a national headline.Since he broke his 26-day fast by accepting soup from health minister Nadda and without the presence of any CJP representative, telltale signs of the organisation's drift from its star draw have emerged. While doubts persist in govt circles over CJP's motives and its insistence on Pradhan's resignation remains a hurdle, govt will not like to give an impression of sacrificing its key figure to street protests but believes that continuing negotiations with the organisation is an enterprise worth its pursuit. Accused of being tone-deaf over the issue of paper leaks and even insensitive to the growing concerns of candidates of competitive exams, govt believes its engagement with and even concessions to CJP's demands, except Pradhan's ouster, will negate the perception.Dipke's own background with AAP and active support he had received from Left organisations mean that a chunk of agitators is unlikely to back down till govt fully concedes. But govt is keen to bridge its gap with a large chunk of apolitical protestors, who have connected with the concerns being espoused by CJP. Modi has taken the lead by announcing fast-track courts to pursue paper leak cases and a bill to make punishment for the guilty stiffer. Termination of 47 officials of NTA, which holds exams like NEET and JEE, and expected reform measures in education are part of that push.
Article Summary: Government is keeping its fingers crossed after its successful attempt to persuade activist Sonam Wangchuk to break his hunger strike. CJP's assertion, though, to continue and even escalate the agitation if its demand for education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation is not met has muddied the waters.

Article Title: The only judges that matter
Article Text: Thirukkural with the Times explores real-world lessons from the classic Tamil text ‘Thirukkural’. Written by Tamil poet and philosopher Thiruvalluvar, the Kural consists of 1,330 short couplets of seven words each. This text is divided into three books with teachings on virtue, wealth, and love and is considered one of the great works ever on ethics and morality. The Kural has influenced scholars and leaders across social, political, and philosophical spheres. Motivational speaker, author and diversity champion Bharathi Bhaskar explores the masterpiece. Every time the winners of a major award are announced, celebrations begin in one corner, controversies in another. The latter often outlives the former. History, however, offers a strange consolation. Awards do not always decide greatness. Time often does. Take Mahakavi Bharathiyar. His immortal poem ‘Senthamizh naadenum pothinile, inba thene vandhu paayudhu kaadhinile’ flows through the veins of every Tamilian today. Yet, when Bharathiyar's friends submitted this poem for a poetry competition, it won only the second prize . Does anyone remember the poem which won the first prize? The irony repeats itself elsewhere. Mahatma Gandhi was nominated several times for the Nobel Peace Prize but never received it. If the apostle of Ahimsa did not fit the definition of a peace laureate, who possibly could? Alfred Hitchcock never won an Oscar despite creating masterpieces like Psycho, Vertigo and Rear Window , films that continue to define the language of cinema. Leo Tolstoy, Virginia Woolf and James Joyce never received the Nobel Prize. Perhaps the most heartbreaking omission was that of Rosalind Franklin. Her pioneering X-ray crystallography images were indispensable to deciphering the structure of DNA. Yet the Nobel Prize in medicine recognised only Watson, Crick and Wilkins. Many readers would remember Jeyamohan's unforgettable short story Yaanai Doctor . Doctor K—modelled on the legendary elephant veterinarian V Krishnamurthy—is recommended for the Padma Shri. Political currents intervene and the honour slips away. That very night, however, a herd of elephants arrives at his doorstep with an injured calf. They have travelled nearly 100km, instinctively searching for the one human they trust. Doctor K quietly treats the animal. What greater recognition can there be than the trust of beings that cannot speak? Some honours are conferred by institutions. Others are bestowed by life itself. These thoughts returned to me while reading the list of the 72nd National Film Awards. Cinema is deeply subjective and different juries value different attributes. Yet many film lovers, myself included, were left perplexed. In my own reckoning, Meiyazhagan deserved to stand among the year's finest films. The film made kindness, innocence and warmth compelling without ever becoming sentimental. Karthi's effortless body language and emotional sincerity became the soul of the film. Maharaja too was a masterclass in layered storytelling. Vijay Sethupathi delivered one of the most restrained performances of his career. Thiruvalluvar expressed a similar sentiment nearly 2,000 years ago, in Kural 849. "Kaanadhaan kaattuvaan; thaan kaanaan. Kaanaadhaan kandaanaam thaan kanda vaaru." “One who presents the unseen as seen will not come forward to see what is to be seen.” Perhaps that is also a gentle reminder of the limits of human judgment. Perhaps another jury , on another day, would have arrived at different conclusions. Awards are human judgments, not eternal truths. Fortunately, artists have always understood something juries forget. Their true audience is not the few who sit around a table but the countless unknown hearts across generations. Rudyard Kipling captured this wisdom in the poem If— : "If you can meet with Triumph and Disaster And treat those two impostors just the same..." Awards and snubs are both impostors. Neither defines an artist. One inflates, the other disappoints; both are temporary. Time is the only jury that never retires. Its verdict may be slow, but it is seldom wrong.
Article Summary: The Kural consists of 1,330 short couplets of seven words each. This text is divided into three books with teachings on virtue, wealth, and love. The Kural has influenced scholars and leaders across social, political, and philosophical spheres.

Article Title: Creation and nurturing of society impossible without motherhood: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat
Article Text:
RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat addresses valedictory session of a two-day national meeting on 'Contemporary Motherhood' organised by Vishwa Mangalya Sabha.

NEW DELHI: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh ( RSS ) chief Mohan Bhagwat on Friday said motherhood is the foundation of creation, nurturing and continuity of society, asserting that "the creation, nurturing and sustenance of the world are impossible without motherhood. "Addressing the valedictory session of a two-day national meeting on "Contemporary Motherhood" organised by Vishwa Mangalya Sabha at the Ambedkar International Centre, Bhagwat said the core principles of motherhood remain timeless even as society changes.He described mothers as a child's first teacher and the primary source of emotional support throughout life, saying they play a decisive role in shaping values and giving the right direction to a person's thinking.Bhagwat said parents should spend more time with their families and maintain open communication with children. He stressed that children learn more through observation than instruction, making it important for parents to lead by example. He also said parents should continue to expand their own knowledge so they can address their children's questions and curiosity.The RSS chief said many debates in society stem from misconceptions, some of which are deliberately created.Referring to Indian culture, he said it had long been portrayed as flawed despite having a strong civilisational foundation. He urged people to move forward with confidence in India's history, traditions and knowledge systems.He also said unity amid diversity lies at the heart of Indian culture and called for strengthening families and social institutions by following Indian cultural values rather than adopting foreign lifestyles without reflection.Bhagwat began his address by saying it was somewhat paradoxical for him to speak on motherhood, adding that women have the primary authority to speak on the subject. He said the organisation had already held extensive discussions on the theme and noted that thinkers such as Swami Vivekananda, Mahatma Gandhi and Rabindranath Tagore had reflected extensively on motherhood and its relevance to society.The event was organised by Vishwa Mangalya Sabha, a women's organisation that says it works towards "nation-building through motherhood." The two-day meeting, held on July 23 and 24, brought together around 280 women from different states to discuss the role of motherhood in the context of changing social conditions and the Indian family system.According to the organisers, more than 900 women attended the concluding session, while between 2,000 and 2,500 women had registered for the dialogue on the theme. The organisation said it held conventions across 23 regions in India in 2026, involving around 37,000 women, and is currently active in 33 regions with nearly six lakh women associated with its activities. It also has a presence in 14 countries, including the United States and the Netherlands.
Article Summary: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh ( RSS ) chief Mohan Bhagwat said motherhood is the foundation of creation, nurturing and continuity of society. He was addressing the valedictory session of a two-day national meeting on "Contemporary Motherhood" organised by Vishwa Mangalya Sabha.

Article Title: RSS women's wing kicks off three-day national meet in Haryana
Article Text:
The meeting commenced with the lighting of a ceremonial lamp, followed by tributes to the organisation's former office-bearers

Organisational review and expansion

Highlights of recent activities

NEW DELHI: The Rashtriya Sevika Samiti, the women's organisation ideologically affiliated with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh ( RSS ), on Friday began its three-day first half-yearly national executive and representatives' meeting at the Madhav Smriti campus in Samalkha, Haryana.Around 500 representatives from 38 provinces are expected to participate in the meeting, which will continue until July 26. The meeting is being attended by Pramukh Sanchalika Shantakkaji and Pramukh Karyavahika Sita Gayatri.The meeting commenced with the lighting of a ceremonial lamp, followed by tributes to the organisation's former office-bearers Rukmini Akka and Rekhatai Raje.Representatives also paid homage to other deceased workers, noted personalities including Asha Bhosle, Suman Kalyanpur and S. Janaki, as well as victims of terrorist attacks, natural disasters and accidents.Addressing the inaugural session, Pramukh Karyavahika Sita Gayatri said the organisation should continue its efforts towards women's empowerment while contributing to nation-building. Referring to the birth anniversary of the organisation's founder Lakshmibai Kelkar, observed as Sankalp Diwas, she called upon members to carry forward the work of the organisation.Sita Gayatri also referred to recent developments, including India's humanitarian medical assistance to Iran, describing it as an example of the country's outreach.She also mentioned India's performance at the International Chemistry Olympiad and the ICC Women's T20 World Cup as indicators of the country's achievements in different fields.The organisation reviewed its activities over the past year, stating that it has expanded its network of branches, meeting centres and service projects.It is currently running service activities at 2,866 locations across the country.These initiatives include projects related to education, value-based learning, self-reliance, healthcare and yoga centres. The organisation also said it operates hostels for girls from remote areas.Around 250 training camps were organised across the country in 2026, in which nearly 15,241 women volunteers received training.The organisation also highlighted several initiatives undertaken during the year. It said volunteers organised a route march in West Bengal after a long gap and referred to a training camp in Jammu where participants continued activities despite heavy rain and strong winds.During a visit to Chhattisgarh, the organisation's chief interacted with women from around 25 different communities as part of a social harmony initiative.It also highlighted the 'Nari Se Narayani' conference organised jointly with the Bharatiya Vidvat Parishad at Vigyan Bhavan in Delhi on International Women's Day.The event was attended by over 1,500 women from across the country, with President Droupadi Murmu addressing the concluding session.The three-day meeting is scheduled to conclude on July 26.
Article Summary: Rashtriya Sevika Samiti is ideologically affiliated with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh. Around 500 representatives from 38 provinces are expected to participate in the meeting. The organisation reviewed its activities over the past year, stating that it has expanded its network.

Article Title: 'That's the world we live in': Travis Head breaks silence on wife's online abuse after Virat Kohli handshake row
Article Text:
Travis Head and Virat Kohli (ANI Photo)

Family affected by online abuse

NEW DELHI: Australia batter Travis Head has spoken publicly for the first time about the controversy involving Virat Kohli during the IPL 2026 match between Sunrisers Hyderabad (SRH) and Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB).The incident gained attention after cameras appeared to show RCB star Kohli skipping a handshake with SRH's Head after the game, leading to speculation about a rift between the two cricketers.Head, however, has dismissed the rumours, saying there was no issue to resolve."I don't think there's anything to patch over. That's just that's what it is. That's yeah. No surprises with how the competition went or what went on. So as expected," Head told Code Sports.The controversy took a personal turn when Head's wife, Jessica Davies, revealed she received abusive messages from fans on social media.Head admitted the online backlash was difficult, especially for his family, although he believes such attention is part of being a professional athlete."I think Jessica and I have a great perspective on things. That's the world we live in, and I think she's amazing in how she handles that kind of stuff.It was more the family stuff was built around it, flowing on to other family members who don't particularly see that sort of stuff," he said.Head also praised his wife for staying calm throughout the episode, adding, "Everyone forgets about it in a few days' time. She handled it extremely well. It's probably handling it with others and what other people's perspective of what things are like."Meanwhile, Kohli's Royal Challengers Bengaluru successfully defended their IPL title by defeating Gujarat Titans in the 2026 final in Ahmedabad.
Article Summary: Travis Head speaks publicly for the first time about controversy involving Virat Kohli. Kohli skipped a handshake with Head after the IPL 2026 match between Sunrisers Hyderabad (SRH) and Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) The incident led to speculation about a rift between the two cricketers.

Article Title: From selling vegetables to e-rickshaw driver, now India's first CWG 2026 medallist: How Bihar's Jhandu Kumar defied all odds
Article Text:
Jhandu Kumar (AP Photo)

From hardship to hope

The breakthrough that changed everything

ALSO READ:

NEW DELHI: For years, Jhandu Kumar's days began at a vegetable market and ended in a gym. When life became tougher during the COVID-19 pandemic, he swapped the market for an e-rickshaw, working long hours to support his family while refusing to give up on his dream of representing India.On Friday in Glasgow, that dream turned into reality.The 28-year-old para powerlifter from Bihar won bronze in the men's heavyweight event at the 2026 Commonwealth Games, claiming India's first para powerlifting medal of the competition.As the medal was placed around his neck, the emotions of years of sacrifice came rushing back."I feel as if I'm flying. This is my first medal. Only one thing was going through my mind: that I have to win the medal. Just have to win," Jhandu told ANI.The journey to the Commonwealth podium was anything but easy.Affected by polio at the age of five, Jhandu battled both physical and financial challenges from an early age. His family's vegetable shop in Harnaut Bazaar, Nalanda district, was forced to shut temporarily during the pandemic due to the construction of an overbridge.To keep the household running, he began driving an e-rickshaw.Yet even then, training remained non-negotiable."Every day I used to travel nearly 20km to Bihar Sharif to buy vegetables, bring them back and sell them in the market. After finishing work around 4 pm, I would go to the gym for training," he had told TOI before the Games.Money was always tight. His daily earnings of Rs 400-500 barely covered household expenses, while protein supplements alone cost nearly Rs 1,000.Eventually, he sold his e-rickshaw in 2023 to compete at the National Para Powerlifting Championships, a gamble that initially failed after he could not register a successful lift.Instead of giving up, Jhandu caught the attention of national coach Rajinder Singh Rahelu, who invited him to train at the Sports Authority of India's National Centre of Excellence in Gandhinagar.That opportunity transformed his career. He went on to win silver at the inaugural Khelo India Para Games, followed by medals at national and international competitions, including bronze at the Asia-Oceania Open Para Powerlifting Championships.In Glasgow, Jhandu lifted 190kg to secure bronze after opening with 181kg. He even attempted a Commonwealth Games record of 196kg in his final lift, but fell just short.Despite missing the record, the medal meant everything."I'm very grateful that they let me practice so much and gave me so much love. I feel very good. I'll try to do even better in the future," he said.He also thanked the Sports Authority of India and the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) for backing his journey."I'm extremely grateful to them. We practice there, and this medal belongs to them, in a way," he said.For Jhandu Kumar, the bronze medal is more than a sporting achievement. It is proof that determination, sacrifice and unwavering belief can lift a person far beyond the weight on the bar.
Article Summary: Jhandu Kumar won bronze in the men's heavyweight event at the 2026 Commonwealth Games. The 28-year-old para powerlifter from Bihar won India's first para powerlifting medal of the competition. Affected by polio at the age of five, Jhandu battled both physical and financial challenges.

Article Title: 'Why is he always retained?': Ashwin fires back at Mayank Yadav's critics
Article Text:
India's bowler Mayank Yadav (AP Photo/Wonder Mashura)

Mayank Yadav's return to international cricket could hardly have gone better, and former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin believes the young fast bowler deserves patience after overcoming a difficult spell with injuries.Playing his first international match since October 2024, Mayank announced his comeback in style during the opening T20I against Zimbabwe in Harare. The speedster was named Player of the Match after producing a match-winning spell that began with a wicket off the very first ball of the contest.Mayank removed Brian Bennett for a duck with a hard-length delivery that straightened after pitching, forcing an outside edge that was safely taken behind the stumps. He continued to test Zimbabwe's batters with his pace and discipline, dismissing Dion Myers during the powerplay to leave the hosts under immediate pressure. His spell laid the platform for India's commanding bowling display.The performance marked a significant moment in the pacer's career after an injury-plagued period stalled his rapid rise. Initially fast-tracked into the Indian side as part of the team's long-term plans for the 2026 T20 World Cup, Mayank spent the past two years battling recurring fitness issues that repeatedly interrupted his progress.Speaking on 'Ash ki Baat', Ashwin reflected on the challenges of returning from multiple injuries and urged fans to avoid judging players too quickly."It is not easy to go through a stress fracture at a young age. We often see and think, why is he always retained? He is always injured. We easily tell this. No player plays to get injured. Injury can be very painful. It is not just physical but also a mental barrier, especially if you are injured twice. It is not easy on the body. If it resurfaces, it plays on your mind. Mayank Yadav has a lot of time and is exceptionally talented. I want him to play more," he said on 'Ash ki Baat'.Ashwin also acknowledged India's convincing start to the series and congratulated new T20I captain Shreyas Iyer on securing his maiden victory as skipper."Congratulations to Shreyas for the first win. He would have been searching for it. There is not a lot to see when you restrict Zimbabwe to 120-odd. Mayank, Prince, and Ashok all got an opportunity," he said.Mayank's impressive return has not only revived India's pace options but also reinforced why he continues to be viewed as one of the country's most exciting fast-bowling prospects when fully fit.
Article Summary: Ravichandran Ashwin believes Mayank Yadav deserves patience after overcoming a difficult spell with injuries. Mayank played his first international match since October 2024 against Zimbabwe. The speedster was named Player of the Match after producing a match-winning spell.

Article Title: Former Indian cricket captain and head coach Rahul Dravid reprises ‘old’ role as hockey enthusiast
Article Text:
Rahul Dravid with former international hockey players Sandeep Somesh (centre) and Anil Aldrin in Bengaluru on Friday

BENGALURU: Rahul Dravid , once a hockey midfielder, famously put away the stick and stuck to weaving magic with the willow. Almost four decades later, with a stick in hand, he can still trap a ball with precision and position a pass well too. The former India captain and coach, who played in the same school team– St. Joseph’s Boys High School– as former international hockey players Anil Aldrin and Sandeep Somesh, counts hockey as one of his favourite sports. Speaking at the opening of the inter-college hockey tournament commemorating the platinum jubilee of his alma mater, St Joseph’s College of Commerce (SJCC), here on Friday, Dravid reminisced about his days on the hockey field.“I played a lot of hockey in school. I was fortunate to play with people like Anil Aldrin and Sandeep Somesh for two reasons. Firstly, we were a strong team and won tournaments like Centenary Shield and the Father Eric Vaz inter-school tournaments because of these two guys. Also, it was a good lesson for me because when I watched them play or played with them, I realised that I was better off playing cricket,” Dravid joked.Incidentally, Dravid and Somesh both played as midfielders, while 1996 Atlanta Olympian Aldrin was a defender. The 53-year-old Dravid said hockey had played an important role in his formative years. “I loved playing hockey. It was a great team sport. India has such an incredible history, legacy and tradition in hockey,” he said.Dravid also praised the resurgence of Indian hockey after the men’s team secured back-to-back Olympic bronze medals in Paris and Tokyo. “We haven’t been able to reach the heights and standards that we had in the past, but I’m glad we have been quite successful in recent times. There is a revival of hockey,” he observed.The two-day five-a-side inter-college hockey tournament, which has attracted 17 teams, has been organised by SJCC’s Old Students’ Association (OSA) and Yes For Hockey. The competition is timely for the revival of collegiate hockey, which has declined over the years.Lauding the efforts of OSA, Dravid said, “They've been very passionate about trying to revive hockey and get more youngsters to play it, which is really important because it's such a phenomenal sport to be a part of. I think it's only going to keep getting better."Known throughout his playing career for exemplifying sportsmanship, Dravid urged young players to uphold the spirit of the game. “Play in the right spirit, competitively but also with the right sense of camaraderie,” he stated, adding, “Not everyone is going to play for the country, but there is so much that sport can give you. The lessons that you learn from sport will carry you for the rest of your life.”
Article Summary: Rahul Dravid counts hockey as one of his favourite sports. Former India captain and coach played in the same school team as former international hockey players Anil Aldrin and Sandeep Somesh. Speaking at the opening of the inter-college hockey tournament commemorating the platinum jubilee of his alma mater, St Joseph’s College of Commerce.

Article Title: 'No question of retirement': BCCI rubbishes speculation over Rohit Sharma's future
Article Text:
Rohit Sharma (ANI Photo)

BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla has firmly rejected rumours over Rohit Sharma 's international future, stating there is "no question" of the India opener retiring at this stage despite growing speculation during the recent England tour.Questions over Rohit's future gathered pace after a prolonged lean patch with the bat, with reports suggesting the third ODI against England at Lord's could potentially be his final appearance for India. However, the 39-year-old answered those doubts in emphatic fashion by smashing 138 off 110 balls, becoming the first Indian batter to score an ODI century at the iconic venue.Speaking to reporters, Shukla rubbished the retirement rumours and insisted there was no truth to the speculation.“Rohit Sharma is a part of our team and is continuing to play. The things being circulated in the media and on social media have no meaning. As of now, there is no question of his retirement,” Shukla said.Rohit's century at Lord's also reinforced his own stance on his future. The India opener has consistently maintained that he wants to continue representing the country and remains determined to secure a place in India's squad for the 2027 ODI World Cup.In an interview with BCCI .tv after his match-winning innings, Rohit made it clear that outside speculation would not distract him from his responsibilities.“My job is with the bat. Come and play, represent my country, represent my team. That's what I have been told to do since my debut so that's what I am going to do,” Rohit said.“The noise since I made my debut was there. And till the time I am going to stay here, it is always going to be there. So it doesn't really matter too much. What matters is what I do on the field, try and contribute to the success of the team. That's all my focus is right now. And let the noise be there. If there is no noise, there is no fun.”Shukla also brushed aside calls for changes in India's leadership group following criticism directed at captain Shubman Gill and head coach Gautam Gambhir .“Everyone is entitled to their opinion, but the decision on who stays in the team and who does not rests with the selectors. The Indian team is performing well and winning matches, so there is no need for any changes at present,” Shukla said.Although Rohit's century at Lord's was one of the highlights of the tour, India finished the United Kingdom leg on a disappointing note. The visitors lost the ODI series against England 2-1 after earlier suffering a 2-0 defeat to Ireland and a 4-0 loss in the T20I series against England.
Article Summary: BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla has rejected rumours over Rohit Sharma's international future. Sharma scored 138 at Lord's to become the first Indian batter to score an ODI century at the iconic venue. The 39-year-old has consistently maintained that he wants to continue representing the country.

Article Title: Tyreek Hill posts an inspiring YouTube video of his rigorous workout and says his timeline is looking really good right now, especially after doctors told him he might not be able to walk again

Article Title: Argentina president Javier Milei breaks silence after 23 million sign petition demanding World Cup ban
Article Text:
Argentine President Javier Milei speaks at the Conservative Political Action Conference in Asuncion, Paraguay, Tuesday, Sept. 16, 2025. (AP Photo/Jorge Saenz)

Petition surpasses 28 million signatures

Spain's Gavi, left, falls as he scuffles with Argentina's Leandro Paredes (5) and Thiago Almada during the World Cup final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Yuki Iwamura)

Milei hits back with defiant social media posts

"Do you have enemies? It means you once defended something. We defend Argentina."

"The problem with Argentina is that we stand out. We don't go unnoticed, people are jealous of us, and we're good at almost everything."

"Long live Argentina, damn it!"

Counter-petition calls for World Cup final replay

Paredes remains unapologetic as FIFA investigation continues

The fallout from Argentina's dramatic 2026 FIFA World Cup final defeat to Spain continues to intensify, with President Javier Milei launching a defiant social media response after an online petition calling for Argentina to be banned from future World Cups surpassed 23 million signatures.Spain claimed their second men's World Cup title with a 1-0 extra-time victory at the New York New Jersey Stadium, where Ferran Torres scored the decisive goal in the 106th minute after Luis de la Fuente's side dominated proceedings and prevented Lionel Messi's Argentina from registering a single shot on target during regular time.However, attention quickly shifted away from the football after chaotic scenes erupted at the final whistle, prompting FIFA to open disciplinary proceedings into the conduct of several members of the Argentina delegation.According to reports, the "Argentina Out" campaign officially closed on 19 July 2026, immediately after the World Cup final, with exactly 23,316,108 verified signatures from supporters across roughly 170 countries. The petition narrowly missed the all-time Guinness World Record for the most-signed online petition, falling just short of the record 24.3 million signatures.The campaign calls on FIFA to exclude Argentina from future World Cups, arguing that the team's conduct during and after the final damaged the image of the sport and calling for stronger action to protect fair play.The petition emerged after a match in which Argentina accumulated repeated fouls, had midfielder Enzo Fernández sent off in stoppage time after receiving a second yellow card, and became involved in an ugly confrontation following Spain's victory.Leandro Paredes was seen grabbing Spain defender Eric García by the throat before clashing with Gavi, while Nahuel Molina appeared to throw a punch toward Spain captain Rodri. FIFA has since launched an investigation into the incidents, with players, coaching staff and the Argentine Football Association potentially facing disciplinary sanctions.Rather than distancing himself from the growing controversy, Argentine President Javier Milei responded with a series of patriotic messages on Instagram defending the national team and criticising what he suggested was hostility toward Argentina.One of the posts shared by the Argentine leader read:In another post, Milei claimed Argentina's global prominence was the reason behind the criticism.He also shared an AI-generated image of himself tearing open his suit to reveal an Argentina shirt underneath, accompanied by the caption:The posts were widely circulated as debate over Argentina's conduct continued both inside and outside the country.The backlash has also fuelled a counter-campaign within Argentina.Thousands of supporters have signed a separate petition demanding the World Cup final be replayed, alleging that Slovenian referee Slavko Vinčić delivered a biased performance favouring Spain.The petition claims the final was influenced by "controversial and corrupt" officiating and asks FIFA to overturn the result.However, no verified evidence has been presented to substantiate those allegations, and there is nothing to indicate that FIFA or Vinčić acted improperly during the match.The Argentine Football Association has also sought to calm speculation surrounding replay demands, while AFA president Claudio "Chiqui" Tapia has urged supporters to accept Spain's victory.The controversy has been compounded by comments from midfielder Leandro Paredes, who has come under intense scrutiny for his role in the post-match altercation.In a social media message published after the final, Paredes expressed pride in Argentina's campaign but stopped short of apologising for his actions."Thank you, Argentina! I love you today and always," he wrote. "Today I write with a lot of pain in my heart because we couldn't give our country the joy it deserved, but with my chest filled with pride for giving everything we had and putting our flag at the top once again."He added that it had been "an honour to be part of the best Argentina team in history."Alongside Paredes, Nahuel Molina, Thiago Almada and assistant coach Roberto Ayala remain under FIFA investigation following the disturbances at MetLife Stadium.Meanwhile, criticism has continued to grow beyond Argentina's borders. Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente recently described the scenes as "intolerable" and praised his players for maintaining their composure throughout the confrontation, while FIFA's disciplinary process remains ongoing as world football's governing body reviews referee reports and video footage from the final.
Article Summary: Petition calling for Argentina to be banned from future World Cups surpasses 23 million signatures. President Javier Milei hits back with defiant social media posts. Spain claimed their second men's World Cup title with a 1-0 extra-time victory at the New York New Jersey Stadium. FIFA has launched disciplinary proceedings into the conduct of several members of the Argentina delegation.

Article Title: Underprepared East Bengal and Mohun Bagan kick-off new season with Durand Cup opener
Article Text:
Mohun Bagan vs East Bengal (PTI Photo)

KOLKATA: India’s oldest football tournament is hours away from an odd and unprecedented beginning. However, kick-starting the Durand Cup with a Kolkata derby for the first time in its 135th-year-old history has its own hype and hazards. Because, the blockbuster match between East Bengal FC and Mohun Bagan SG at the Salt Lake Stadium on Saturday will also set in motion the start of India’s domestic football season as well and the hard truth is that both teams look oddly underprepared.Let’s fix our gaze on some strange layers of the match. ISL champions East Bengal and runners-up Mohun Bagan — now under new coaches Antonio Lopez Habas and Panagiotis Dilmperis respectively — have hit the training ground running only four days ago. Not to mention the fact that while Habas will have only newcomer Dani Ramirez and old hand Mohammad Rashid available for selection, Dilmperis’ cupboard looks emptier with Serbian forward Dejan Drazic being the only foreigner to take part in Friday’s pre-match training session — a strange departure from the past when overseas players have predominantly emerged as show-stealers in such duels. It’s somewhat fitting that domestic players will now get the kind of spotlight they are rarely granted, thereby giving this season-opening derby primarily an indigenous spine."We haven't had enough time to train. It's impossible to prepare properly for such an important match in just a few days,” Habas admitted on Friday. "Our idea is to make the team solid, compact and competitive. We need time to develop our model of play, but that's the foundation we want to build," he added.It’s a strange but emotionally-charged homecoming for the 69-year-old Spaniard, who holds a rare link to the inaugural season of ISL and has guided now defunct ATK to two titles and Mohun Bagan to an ISL winner’s Shield.“I have absolute respect for Mohun Bagan and for everything we achieved together. I have wonderful memories of the fans and my time in Kolkata. But now I have another job, another responsibility. I have to fight for my new team," Habas said.His counterpart, Dilmperis — fondly called Panos — is also bracing for a challenging debut. Having made his mark as Punjab FC coach, the 51-year-old Greek couldn’t have asked for a toucher test for his coronation as Bagan coach.“Starting my journey with a derby is exciting because this is why football exists. Football is about rivalries, competition, and passion. Joining a club like Mohun Bagan, with its incredible fan base, rich history, ambitious ownership, and high expectations, is not pressure for me—it is a huge source of motivation," Panos remarked.“For me, every match is a derby. Whether we are playing the team at the top of the table or the bottom, I prepare with the same intensity,” he maintained.The last time a domestic tournament began with a derby happened way back in the 2004-2005 season of I-League. However, by that time, both teams had already gone through the grind of the local league.Starved of adequate time to pass muster, both teams are facing a whole new ball game. The likes of Bipin Singh, Edmund Lalrindika and David Lalhlansanga in the upfront as well as Jeakson Singh and Anwar Ali in defence contributed immensely to East Bengal’s march to the ISL summit last season. They will again be tasked with a new challenge of rising to the occasion.For Bagan, Liston Colaco, Manvir Singh and Sahal Abdul Samad will again be central to the team’s ambitions.However, it may threaten to float away into its own strange space; this season-opening derby with essentially a rare desi look will have the odds stacked against no team. It’s floating along the usual 50-50 narrative.
Article Summary: The Durand Cup kicks off with a Kolkata derby for the first time in its 135th- year-old history. ISL champions East Bengal and runners-up Mohun Bagan have hit the training ground running only four days ago. Both teams look oddly underprepared.

Article Title: India eye series win vs Zimbabwe: Can Abhishek Sharma break his lean run?
Article Text:
Abhishek Sharma (ANI Photo)

After the bruising their T20 side endured on the UK tour, this Zimbabwe series could be just the ideal fillip India needed.Having finally recorded their maiden win under new T20 captain Shreyas Iyer after seven winless matches at the helm, India will look to secure an unassailable 2-0 lead when they take on Zimbabwe in the second T20I at the Harare Sports Club on Saturday.Following a difficult run that saw them whitewashed by Ireland (0-2) and England (0-4), India’s convincing sevenwicket victory in the seriesopener has restored some much-needed confidence.Yet, even as the visitors look to build on that momentum, one player who will be under the scanner is explosive opener Abhishek Sharma.Two years ago, Harare was the venue where Abhishek announced himself on the international stage with a breathtaking maiden T20I hundred in only his second game.The stylish left-hander returns to the same ground searching for a spark after a worrying dip in form. Having begun the England series promisingly with scores of 59 and 43, Abhishek’s returns thereafter have read 10, 16, 3 and 1. In Thursday’s opener, his uncomfortable eight-ball 1 suggested a batter short on rhythm and confidence.With competition for places intensifying, Abhishek knows he needs runs. Senior opener Sanju Samson, though absent on this tour, remains in the selectors’ plans and has been named in India’s squad for the Asian Games later this year.A substantial score in Harare would not only help India seal the series but also strengthen Abhishek’s own case in a rapidly evolving T20 setup.India, though, found a new hero in the opening match.Teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi smashed a stunning 18-ball fifty, becoming the youngest player to score a T20I half-century.The 15-year-old, who had endured a difficult England tour where pacy bowlers like Jofra Archer tested him relentlessly with short-pitched bowling, responded in style against Zimbabwe.Taking on Richard Ngarava and Blessing Muzarabani fearlessly, he produced a blistering innings that underlined why he is so highly rated.Supported by Ishan Kishan’s brisk 35 and an unbeaten 28 from skipper Iyer, Sooryavanshi ensured India chased down the target with more than six overs to spare.Head coach VVS Laxman would have been equally pleased by the performance of India’s revamped pace attack. The biggest positive was the return of Mayank Yadav, who made an impressive comeback after two injury-ravaged years. The Delhi quick finished with figures of 2 for 18 and consistently touched high speeds, with his opening delivery to Brian Bennett at 150 kmph indidcating that his pace remains intact.Prince Yadav also showed signs of improvement after a lean England tour, while debutant Ashok Sharma displayed enough promise to suggest he could become another exciting fast-bowling option.
Article Summary: India will look to secure an unassailable 2-0 lead when they take on Zimbabwe in the second T20I at the Harare Sports Club on Saturday. The stylish left-hander returns to the same ground searching for a spark after a worrying dip in form. Teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi smashed a stunning 18-ball fifty.

Article Title: India's Sainyam settles for 10m pistol silver at Shooting World Cup in China
Article Text:
Sainyam

PUNE: Sainyam Vij missed the gold by just 0.2 points as she shrugged off multiple challenges from Olympic medallists, the world No. 1, her teammate and two local shooters at the ISSF World Cup in Hangzhou, China, on Friday.The Chandigarh girl clinched silver in the women’s 10m air pistol category after finishing behind reigning World No. 1 and World Champion shooter Qianxun Yao of China in the final.Sainyam scored 243.4 in the final, while Yao shot to gold with 243.6, while the bronze went to Iran’s Haniyeh Rostamiyan, who scored 221.On her way to the silver, Sainyam left Paris Games gold medallist Yejin Oh of Korea (8th), Tokyo Games double medallist Ranxin Jiang of China (5th) and her teammate Suruchi Phogat (7th) behind.“It was a good medal to win. I was not thinking about the field. For me the field was neither tough nor weak as I was focused on my own shooting,” Sainyam told TOI after winning the medal.

Article Title: Quote of the day by David Beckham: "I have always believed that if you want to achieve anything special in life you have to…" - a powerful lesson on hard work, discipline and why talent alone is never
Article Text:
David Beckham

Quote of the day by David Beckham

"I have always believed that if you want to achieve anything special in life you have to work, work, and then work some more"

What is the meaning behind David Beckham’s quote

Why talent alone rarely gets someone all the way there

Why setbacks tested this philosophy directly

Why consistency matters more than occasional motivation

Other famous quotes by David Beckham

"The secret to my success is practice!"

"The secret of the team's success is easy, unity and hard work."

"You will go through tough times, it's about getting through them."

"I don't have time for hobbies. At the end of the day, I treat my job as a hobby. It's something I love doing."

Why it still feels relevant today

People tend to admire success from a safe distance, seeing the trophy without ever seeing the years that produced it. David Beckham summed up his own version of that gap plainly. "I have always believed that if you want to achieve anything special in life you have to work, work, and then work some more," he said. The repetition is not accidental. He is describing something continuous, not a single burst of effort that happens once and then stops. Coming from a player often remembered for his technique on free kicks and crosses, the line carries the weight of someone who actually built that skill through repetition, rather than someone simply repeating a motivational slogan he never had to test himself. His journey from a young academy player to a global football icon reflects the discipline, patience and relentless commitment required to turn natural ability into lasting excellence on the biggest stages. The quote serves as a timeless reminder that extraordinary achievements are rarely the result of talent alone, but of consistent effort sustained long after the initial excitement has faded.The phrase "anything special in life" is deliberately broad, applying just as easily to a career in business or medicine as it does to professional sport. The answer he gives is repeated three times for a reason, work, work, work some more, because Beckham is not describing hard work as an occasional event.He is describing it as the actual, unglamorous rhythm behind lasting achievement.Natural ability offers a real head start, but plenty of gifted people never fully develop it, while plenty of less naturally talented people outwork their way past them over time. Former teammates and coaches have repeatedly described Beckham staying behind after regular training to practise free kicks and crosses long after everyone else had gone home, which is really the practical version of the quote in action.Beckham faced serious public criticism at points in his career, most famously after being sent off during England's 1998 World Cup exit to Argentina. He later described that period bluntly. "I have nightmares about France 98," he said. "It was humiliating. It will always be with me." Rather than letting that moment define the rest of his career, he kept working and went on to become one of England's most recognised footballers, a direct example of the same principle behind today's quote.Motivation naturally rises and falls, strong some days and completely absent on others. Discipline is what keeps someone working through the days motivation does not show up, which is really the difference between an ambition that stays an idea and one that eventually becomes a career.Modern culture often makes success look instant, a single viral moment or a sudden breakthrough. Beckham's own career is a reminder that most of what actually produces lasting results happens quietly, well before anyone else is paying attention, repeated on ordinary days long after the initial excitement of starting has worn off.
Article Summary: "I have always believed that if you want to achieve anything special in life you have to work, work, and then work some more" - David Beckham. The quote serves as a timeless reminder that extraordinary achievements are rarely the result of talent alone. Beckham's own career is a reminder that most of what produces lasting results happens quietly.

Article Title: North Carolina spent 25 years rebuilding an elk population that had disappeared from the state; in 2027, it will allow its first limited hunt with just two permits
Article Text:
Elk were once found across much of North Carolina but disappeared from the state many years ago

The hunt

Elk in western North Carolina. (Photos: WLOS)

The permits

The rules

For the first time since elk were reintroduced to western North Carolina 25 years ago, the state will allow a limited elk hunting season. The decision comes after wildlife officials said the elk population has recovered enough to support controlled hunting while continuing conservation efforts.The change follows the signing of House Bill 747 by North Carolina Governor Josh Stein on July 7. The law allows the North Carolina Wildlife Resources Commission (NCWRC) to issue two elk hunting permits during the 2027 hunting season.Officials say the move is not aimed at reducing the population quickly but is part of a long-term wildlife management plan. The money raised through the permits will also be used for elk conservation and management.Elk were once found across much of North Carolina but disappeared from the state many years ago because of overhunting and habitat loss. Wildlife agencies later began efforts to bring them back to western North Carolina, and the animals have slowly established a stable population over the past 25 years.According to Justin McVey, district wildlife biologist with the NCWRC, the state has now reached an important milestone."Our goal for elk management in the state is to have a sustainable huntable population and at this point we've reached that goal," McVey said, as quoted by ABC 13 news.A sustainable population means there are enough animals to maintain healthy numbers while also allowing a limited number to be hunted without affecting the long-term survival of the species.The state is taking a cautious approach by issuing only two permits during the first hunting season. The two permits will be distributed in different ways.One permit will be auctioned through a wildlife conservation non-profit organisation that took part in the elk reintroduction programme in North Carolina.Under the law, the selected non-profit can keep up to 25% of the auction proceeds. The remaining money will go towards wildlife conservation.The second permit will be issued through a public raffle. Raffle tickets will cost $20 each, and participants can buy up to 30 tickets for $500. To enter, buyers must have a valid North Carolina hunting licence or be eligible for a licence exemption under state regulations.The Wildlife Resources Commission may receive up to $25,000 from the raffle proceeds. The rest of the money collected from both the auction and raffle will be deposited into the state's Wildlife Resources Fund, where it will be used for elk conservation and management programmes.McVey said the permits are expected to become available in July 2027. The elk hunting season is scheduled to begin later that year in October.Hunters who receive permits will be allowed to hunt in areas within the state's designated elk zone where elk are present."They'll be able to basically hunt any area in the elk zone that has elk; it'll be private land as well as game lands," McVey said.However, anyone planning to hunt on private property must first obtain permission from the landowner.Wildlife officials also said that hunters must follow all state hunting regulations. Those who violate the rules could face fines or other penalties.In addition, every elk harvested during the season must be reported to the NCWRC and presented to the agency as required under the new law.
Article Summary: Elk were once found across much of North Carolina but disappeared from the state many years ago because of overhunting and habitat loss. Wildlife agencies later began efforts to bring them back to western North Carolina, and the animals have slowly established a stable population over the past 25 years.

Article Title: Archaeologists uncover rare 2,000-year-old Liubo game boards in Han Dynasty tombs, but its rules remain one of history's greatest mysteries
Article Text:
Image: AI Generated

Rare Liubo game boards discovered inside Han Dynasty tombs

What was Liubo, and why are its rules still unknown

Archaeology suggests Liubo was played at banquets as well as in tombs

Why Liubo remains one of archaeology's greatest unsolved puzzles

Centuries before chess spread across Asia, another board game captivated people throughout ancient China. Known as Liubo, it was played by emperors, nobles and ordinary families during the Han Dynasty, appearing so frequently that complete game sets were buried alongside the dead. Yet despite its popularity more than 2,000 years ago, the game's rules have almost entirely vanished. A recent archaeological discovery of rare Liubo game boards carved into Han Dynasty tombs has renewed interest in one of China's greatest historical mysteries. The find not only highlights the game's importance in everyday life and burial traditions but also underscores a remarkable paradox: archaeologists know what the board looked like, what pieces players used and where the game was played, yet no one can say with certainty how a match actually unfolded.Archaeologists identified two Liubo boards engraved directly onto square bricks inside Han Dynasty tombs dating to around 2,000 years ago. The discovery formed part of a larger excavation that also revealed pottery figurines, ceramic vessels and other funerary objects.Although Liubo boards have been discovered before, archaeologists rarely find them preserved in their original burial context. Their placement inside tombs suggests the game held lasting significance beyond recreation.During the Han Dynasty (206 BCE–220 CE), objects interred with the deceased often reflected activities or possessions considered valuable in the afterlife.Evidence from the Metropolitan Museum of Art supports this interpretation. Its well-preserved Liubo Board and Pieces, dating from the 1st century BCE–1st century CE, includes gaming pieces made from earthenware and bone. The museum notes that Liubo was "a popular game in the Han dynasty" and that such sets embodied wishes for the continuation of life after death.Liubo emerged no later than the Warring States period and remained one of China's most widely played board games for several centuries before gradually disappearing after the Han Dynasty.Players competed on a square board decorated with a distinctive TLV pattern, using gaming pieces and throwing six casting sticks or, in some versions, dice, to determine movement. Beyond these basic elements, certainty quickly disappears.In his influential study, ‘ A Tricky Game: A Re-evaluation of Liubo Based on Archaeological and Textual Evidence ,’ Dr Armin Selbitschka of Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich argues that modern scholarship has often overstated the game's supposed mystical or divinatory nature. After examining archaeological discoveries alongside surviving historical texts, he concludes that Liubo was primarily a game of entertainment, even though symbolic and religious associations emerged in certain regions during the later Eastern Han period.Crucially, no ancient instruction manual explaining the rules has survived. Historians have proposed several reconstructions based on excavated boards, gaming pieces and literary references, but none has achieved scholarly consensus. As a result, Liubo remains one of the few major ancient board games whose equipment is well documented while its gameplay remains largely unknown.The new discovery fits a broader archaeological pattern seen across Han Dynasty China. Selbitschka's research examined dozens of excavated tombs containing Liubo equipment and found that game boards frequently appeared alongside food vessels, drinking cups, musical instruments and figurines. Rather than representing isolated ritual objects, these groupings resemble scenes of banquets and social gatherings recreated inside tombs.The study argues that Liubo occupied an important place in elite entertainment. Historical writings by authors such as Sima Qian also refer to the game in descriptions of court life, competitions and leisure, reinforcing archaeological evidence that it was a familiar pastime rather than an obscure ceremonial practice.This interpretation contrasts with older theories that viewed Liubo mainly as a tool for divination because of the board's distinctive TLV design. According to Selbitschka, archaeological evidence indicates that recreational play remained its principal role throughout most of the Western Han period.Few ancient games present such an unusual challenge to historians. Archaeologists have uncovered exquisitely crafted lacquered boards, ceramic playing pieces, bronze fittings, carved stone examples and complete Liubo sets from royal mausoleums, aristocratic burials and Han Dynasty tombs across China. Museums, including the Metropolitan Museum of Art, preserve these remarkable artefacts. Paintings, stone reliefs and funerary objects even depict people gathered around Liubo boards, confirming that it was far more than an obscure pastime.A carved board inside a Han Dynasty tomb or a complete gaming set recovered from an ancient burial may appear modest compared with spectacular treasures of gold or jade, yet each provides another clue about a game that dominated Chinese society for centuries before disappearing almost completely by the end of the Tang Dynasty. Future excavations may eventually uncover an illustrated manual, an inscribed game board or a more detailed written account capable of solving the mystery.Until then, Liubo remains one of archaeology's most intriguing unsolved puzzles. It is a rare example of a game whose equipment, artwork and cultural significance have survived for more than two millennia, while the knowledge required to play it has quietly slipped out of history.
Article Summary: Rare Liubo game boards discovered inside Han Dynasty tombs. Archaeologists identified two Liubos engraved directly onto square bricks. The discovery formed part of a larger excavation that also revealed pottery figurines, ceramic vessels and other funerary objects. The find highlights the game's importance in everyday life.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit







El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El Rubius was eliminated from MrBeast's $1 million streamer challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.

Article Title: IPL craze costs techie Rs 1.46 lakh in fake RCB vs CSK ticket scam
Article Text:
Image credit: AI generated pic

RCB register their second win

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think the demand for IPL tickets is too high every season? Yes, it's excessive. No, it's just right. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: IPL comes and the demand for tickets and passes go soaring up by the fans. The desperation to get inside the stadium to watch their favourite teams in action in the IPL go high and high. When the tickets get sold out, the demand gets too hig, and the cricket fans even ask for tickets in black. But for a 25-year-old techie the craze for IPL tickets for RCB vs CSK turned too costly and he was duped for a massive Rs. 1.46 lakh.The techie, a resident of B Narayanapura, fell into a trap by a post posted by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram.As per a report in Deccan Herald, the techie alleged in a complaint to Mahadevapura Police that an individual claiming to be Sumit Biswal promised he could arrange IPL tickets along with food coupons.As per the techie, Biswal was introduced him as a senior supervisor for ticket counter at M Chinnaswamy Stadium"He asked me to come near the stadium gate number 10, saying someone would deliver the tickets within minutes, and even sent an email confirmation to gain my trust," the complainant told Deccan Herald."Initially, I agreed to buy two tickets for Rs 3,700 each,but he kept asking for more money under various pretexts such as refundable security deposits, additional ID cards and food coupons.Trusting him, I made multiple payments - even using my mother’s bank account after exhausting my own limits—and ended up transferring around Rs 1.46 lakh," he added.Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s incisive spell of 3-41, coming after a marauding batting show from Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal, propelled Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to a commanding 43-run victory over Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in their IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday.The contest saw RCB’s batting unit dismantle CSK’s attack with relentless hitting, as David’s 70 not out off just 25 balls and Patidar’s unbeaten 48 off only 19 balls provided for the late fireworks after Padikkal’s fluent 50 off 29 balls had set the tone for the daunting total.Their combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026. In reply, CSK faltered under scoreboard pressure, with Sarfaraz Khan’s 50 off 24 balls and Prashant Veer’s 43 the lone acts of resistance amid a string of failures from the top order.Bhuvneshwar was at his disciplined best and even crossed the 200-mark in terms of wickets in IPL, with others also chipping in as CSK were bowled out for 207 in 19.4 overs. The comprehensive win also meant RCB have registered four consecutive triumphs over CSK for the first time in the IPL’s history.
Article Summary: Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) beat Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday. Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal put on a marauding batting show to lift RCB to a daunting 250/3. RCB have registered four consecutive triumphs over CSK for the first time in the IPL’s history.

Article Title: Clavicular Viral Controversy: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends







The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.
Article Summary: A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration.
