Article Title: 3,000 brave rain & threat of crackdown, converge on Shivaji Park
Article Text:
People from all walks of life participated in the protest

Mumbai:

(With inputs from S Ahmed Ali)





Under a heavy overcast sky and oppressive mid-monsoon humidity, Shivaji Park in Dadar witnessed a massive crowd—of roughly 3,000 protesters by police’s estimate—on the sixth day of student-led demonstrations in the city on Friday.Police lodged an FIR against five persons for participating in demonstrations in Shivaji Park as well as Tilak Nagar in Chembur and Santacruz in defiance of prohibitory orders on large public gatherings.The protest at Shivaji Park was scheduled to begin at 4pm, but it was swarming with imposing numbers well before the opening call, transforming Dadar into the epicentre of a growing youth movement. A central stage was erected for speakers, positioned under the gaze of the Meenatai Thackeray bust near the park’s main entrance. Unlike most protests that feature a loud protester with a ‘dafli’, this one had a set playlist: patriotic songs, songs from the movie ‘Rang De Basanti’, and track ‘Azaadi’ from ‘Gully Boy’.Within moments of commencement, the human tide stretched from the junction outside Shiv Sena Bhavan to the park gates. Police vans lined the main thoroughfares and the final stretch of Keluskar Road leading into the park was barricaded.Several protesters scrambled onto bollards and surrounding residential boundary walls to secure a vantage view of the stage.Attendees held placards like “Lathis are for criminals, why use them on students?” and “Everybody is gangsta until cockroaches start flying”. Adding to the visual spectacle, several young demonstrators arrived in full cosplay—including Captain America, Krrish, and a wildly popular Spider-Man.Interspersed throughout the dense crowd were people from all walks of life, brought together by shared frustration over exam leaks and crackdowns.Dr Adarsh Tajane (24), an intern at Sion Hospital who arrived straight from work in his medical scrubs and stethoscope, emphasised the need for systemic reform. “An example needs to be set for the future so that things like paper leaks don’t happen,” he said.For others, the motivation was personal. Dr Disha Vichare, a dentist wrapped in the Tricolour and holding a red rose, drew on her own experience with competitive exams. “I have been through NEET and understand the mental toll it can take,” she said. “Those students did not have to die, and moreover, people were beaten up for raising the issue.”The protest also drew first-time agitators like Shreesti Kumari (27), a copywriter originally from Jharkhand. She said police action against students in Delhi was the tipping point that pushed her out onto the street.Student Balraj Singh (19) stood holding a compilation of Bhagat Singh ’s writings. “He stood for change,” he said.Broader solidarity brought cross-generational participation from across the city. Murtaza Engineer, an advocate in Bombay high court, arrived from Mazgaon with his wife, brother and 81-year-old mother. “My daughter is a surgeon at JJ Hospital. I don’t need to be here, but this is for the children of India,” he said. “My daughter has already cleared the exam, but we are asking for accountability. We shouldn’t need to protest for that. ”Around 6.15pm, police personnel began slowly nudging the crowd out of the primary assembly zone. As the main gathering dispersed, smaller groups split off into surrounding feeder roads, briefly stalling traffic across Dadar.
Article Summary: Police lodged an FIR against five persons for participating in demonstrations in Shivaji Park as well as Tilak Nagar in Chembur and Santacruz. People from all walks of life, brought together by shared frustration over exam leaks and crackdowns.

Article Title: Kolhapur must unite to groom new olympians inspired by Khashaba: Tejaswini Sawant
Article Text:
Kolhapur

:





A consensus emerged at a sports seminar on Thursday, held to mark the 74th anniversary of Olympian Khashaba Jadhav’s historic Olympic medal, that sports associations, the govt, industry and society must work together to produce future Olympic medallists inspired by Jadhav’s legacy.The 74th Medal Day was celebrated for the first time in Kolhapur at the Shri Datta Sports Complex under the joint aegis of the Raje Salunkhe Chalukya Rajvansh Pratishthan and the Kolhapur District and City Wrestling Association. A commemorative poster for the 75th anniversary (Amrit Mahotsav) of Jadhav’s Olympic medal was unveiled.Olympian shooter Tejaswini Sawant said, “There is no shortage of talent in Kolhapur. However, athletes should compete with themselves rather than with others. They should strive to improve themselves by one % every day. One should not give up even in the case of failure. Success comes through the values instilled by parents, honest hard work, and consistency. The love and support Kolhapur residents show for athletes is a great strength, and this energy must be passed on to the new generation. ”Former Kolhapur District Cricket Association president Bal Patankar said sports culture must become part of every household.“One does not need an official position to work in the sports sector. It is important to set aside differences between associations and ensure facilities are available to athletes. There should be effective utilization of CSR funds alongside the Central Government’s sports budget; however, sports associations must maintain transparency to achieve this,” he said.Kolhapur District and City Wrestling Association president Ravindra Patil said the city needed a state-of-the-art indoor wrestling stadium. “If substantial funds are provided for the development of talims (traditional wrestling arenas) and if wrestling receives royal-style patronage once again, a wrestler from Kolhapur could win an Olympic gold medal in the future.”Shivaji Salunkhe, president of the Raje Salunkhe Chalukya Rajvansh Pratishthan, and sports analyst and author Prof. Sanjay Dudhane also addressed the gathering.The seminar, titled “Plans and Initiatives to Produce Another Khashaba in Kolhapur,” also saw the distribution of 75 commemorative posters, designed by Prof. Dudhane, to talims and schools ahead of the 75th anniversary of Jadhav’s Olympic medal win.
Article Summary: The 74th Medal Day was celebrated for the first time in Kolhapur at the Shri Datta Sports Complex. A commemorative poster for the 75th anniversary (Amrit Mahotsav) of Jadhav’s Olympic medal was unveiled.

Article Title: 4 held for theft of 17 kg silver mask, cladding of Shivling at historic temple in Maharashtra's Khopoli
Article Text:
Khopoli police arrested four burglars for stealing silver items from a historic temple





NAVI MUMBAI: The Khopoli police in Raigad detected the burglary at the 18th century historic Shree Vireshwar temple, where 17 kg silver mask and silver cladding on Shivling was stolen on July 19 past midnight around 2 am, by arresting four accused burglars on Tuesday.The arrested accused are Amol Kasbe (36) and Vikas Agiwale (25), who were arrested from Shirur, Pune district and Dilip Jadhav (40) and Sakharam Gaikwad (40), who were arrested from Parner in Ahilyanagar district.The 17 kg silver mask and cladding on the Shivling was adorned in 2023 for which the around Rs 28 lakhs expenses were borne by the temple's trust from the donations received from devotees.Sachin Hire, senior inspector of Khopoli said, "On July 19, the assistant priest at the temple identified as Kishore Shigwan (56) lodge a complaint that the silver mask and cladding on Shivling was stolen. The thieves had entered the temple by breaking the chain and lock of the rear gate, which always remained close as the devotees were allowed entry only from the front gate.""Upon checking CCTV camera footage at the temple, it was seen that four masked men had entered the sanctum sanctorum around 2 am and decamped with the silver mask and cladding on the Shivling. Subsequently, an FIR was registered under BNS sections for house tres-pass, theft in a dwelling house and joint criminal liability. "Inspector Hire said, "Multiple teams were formed to trace the gang of burglars.Using technical expertise and informer network, we zeroed-in on four history-sheeters. They were traced to Pune and Ahilyanagar district and gradually apprehended on Tuesday.""They have revealed the place where they have hidden the stolen silver mask and cladding. Accordingly, a police team will recover the stolen valuables. Previously, there are criminal cases of theft and robbery registered against the arrested accused in Ahilyanagar and Pune districts."
Article Summary: The 17 kg silver mask and cladding on the Shivling was adorned in 2023 for which the around Rs 28 lakhs expenses were borne by the temple's trust. The arrested accused are Amol Kasbe, Vikas Agiwale, Dilip Jadhav and Sakharam Gaikwad.

Article Text:
Unidentified man booked for sexually assaulting female stray dog (Representative image generated using AI)





NAVI MUMBAI: A 31-year-old woman advocate, who is a dog lover, has registered an FIR at Ulwe police station against an unidentified man aged 30-35 years for allegedly sexually assaulting a female stray dog and causing injury to her private part.The incident occurred outside a tea shop on the ground floor in Siddhivinayak Platinum society in sector 23, Ulwe on Sunday around 11.45pm.Acting on a complaint by Advocate Gayatri Khanvilkar, a resident of the said building, the unidentified accused was booked under BNS section and Prevention of Cruelty to Animal.Adv Khanvilkar said, "As per my daily routine, on Sunday night, I went downstairs to feed the stray dogs loitering near our building. It was raining heavily and pitch darkness due to defunct streetlight poles.""I pucker whistled to call the dogs, when a female stray dog, who had delivered puppies last month, came out from behind a plastic table kept horizontally lying on the floor outside the closed tea shop next to the building's main gate. I could see a man hiding behind the table. I became suspicious and asked him what he was doing.""The man ran away semi-naked with his trouser and underwear in his hand.I chased him but taking advantage of the darkness amid heavy rains, he escaped towards the highway."She added, "I called my father downstairs after informing about the incident. We closely checked the dog and found her bleeding from private part. Also, there was human semen on the floor behind the table. I fed the dog and contacted a volunteer of an NGO Jeevan Foundation Yuva Sena, Animal Welfare Force in Kharghar.""I arranged a cab for the volunteer, who took the injured dog to Panvel Panchayat Samiti's Animal Husbandry department, opposite Panvel ST bus depot, where the government veterinarian confirmed sexual assault on the dog, who was treated for the injuries. Hence, I registered an FIR against the unidentified accused man for sexually assaulting the female stray dog and causing injury to her private part.""Our building's CCTV footage shows the accused man running away from the building, but just because the street lights were not working, his image was not clearly visible. We are retrieving more CCTV footages from other shops in our building for providing them to Ulwe police."PSI Rama Dhavare of Ulwe said, "After registering an FIR, the forensic team collected the human semen sample and hair strands from the crime scene. Once the accused is arrested, the DNA match will be the vital evidence in court for conviction of the accused."
Article Summary: The incident occurred outside a tea shop on the ground floor in Siddhivinayak Platinum society in sector 23, Ulwe on Sunday around 11.45pm. The unidentified accused was booked under BNS section and Prevention of Cruelty to Animal.

Article Title: 9 woman rescued from flesh trade in Taloja lodge, 3 accused held
Article Text:
The crime branch team arrested three accused including the lodge manager and two waiters.

NAVI MUMBAI: The Anti-Human Trafficking Unit (AHTU) of Navi Mumbai crime branch busted a prostitution racket at hotel-cum lodge in Taloja and rescued nine women from the flesh trade on July 18. The crime branch team arrested three accused including the lodge manager and two waiters.Gajanan Kadam, senior inspector of AHTU said, "As per the information received about prostitution being carried out at Hotel Abode Inn Lodging and Boarding in Taloja, we set a trap by sending a decoy customer, whom the lodge manager provided a woman for sexual favour for Rs 3,000 that was accepted by one waiter. On the signal of the customer customer, we raided the lodge, where 9 women were kept for prostitution. The lodge manager Balram Gowda, waiters Girish Pujari and Krishnaraj Patil were arrested for dragging the women into prostitution. An FIR was registered at Taloja police station against the three arrested accused Gowda, Pujari and Patil, who were booked relevant BNS sections and Prevention of Immoral Trafficking Act. The Panvel court remanded them to police custody till July 21. The rescued women were sent to women's shelter home as directed by the magistrate."
Article Summary: The Anti-Human Trafficking Unit of Navi Mumbai crime branch busted a prostitution racket at hotel-cum lodge in Taloja. The crime branch team arrested three accused including the lodge manager and two waiters. The lodge manager Balram Gowda, waiters Girish Pujari and Krishnaraj Patil were arrested.

Article Title: 63-year-old shepherd held with charas worth Rs 35L in Raigad
Article Text:
The arrested accused was identified as Sadik Abrahim Shekhdare, a resident of Shekhadi village

NAVI MUMBAI: A 63-year-old shepherd was arrested by Shrivardhan police in Raigad after he was caught in possession of 2.146 kgs of charas worth Rs 10.73 lakhs after laying a trap on July 18 on a tip off that he was selling charas.In his police custody remand till July 22, he led the cops to an discarded boat where he had hidden more quantity of charas which was found weighing 6.996 kgs estimated worth Rs 24.25 lakh. Hence, the total seized contraband was worth Rs 34.98 lakh.The arrested accused was identified as Sadik Abrahim Shekhdare, a resident of Shekhadi village, Shrivardhan taluka. An FIR under NDPS Act was registered against him at Shrivardhan police station on July 19.Surendra Garad, police inspector of Shrivardhan said, "The arrested accused Shekhdare claimed that he had found the charas sachets on Shekhadi beach in Shrivardhan taluka in Aug 2023, when 107 charas packets were found washed ashore at different beaches across Raigad district. The drugs packets washed ashore were labelled as 'Afghan Product'. It was then speculated that the narcotics packets were likely being smuggled by drug traffickers via sea routes, when either the packets fell into the sea or the vessel transporting them may have capsized at an unknown location in the middle of the sea.Due to high tides, the narcotics packets drifted and washed up on the shores of different beaches in the Raigad district."PI Garad said, "The accused Shekhdare was apprehended after laying a trap on the stretch of road from Shekhadi to Aaravi villages, near a crematorium at Kondivali village. As he came riding on a bike, our police team intercepted him. When his bike's dickey was checked, we found two packets containing Charas and after interrogating him in police custody remand, he led us to more quantity of Charas, he had hidden in a boat. "Meanwhile, in August 2023, after over 10kg of charas in nine sachets bearing the label 'Afghan Product' was found at Shrivardhan beach, there were incidents of several plastic packets containing Charas washing up on Raigad beaches. The narcotics were estimated to be worth around Rs 41.54 lakh.The Raigad police initiated a search operation after more than 250kg of narcotics in plastic packets had washed up on the beaches of Kadre, Ladghar, Kelshi, Kolthale, Murud, Burundi, and Dabhol in Dapoli taluka of Ratnagiri district from August 14 to August 17, 2023. Members of the fishing community and coastal security guards were alerted to be vigilant in case they discovered suspicious packets along the shore.As the Raigad police continued the search operation, a total of 98 plastic packets of charas were found washed up on Maral and Kondivali beaches in Shrivardhan taluka, as well as on Sarvesagar and Diveagar beaches within the jurisdiction of the Dighi coastal police station. A total of 30 plastic sachets of charas were found on Maral beach in Srivardhan taluka. They weighed 35.549kg and estimated around Rs 1.42 crore in the international market.On the same day, 24 plastic sachets of charas, weighing 26.751 kgs and valued at around Rs 1.07 crore, were found on Dighi coastal Sarvesagar beach. The next day evening, 11 plastic sachets of charas were found on Kondivali beach in Srivardhan taluka, and 33 packets were discovered on Dighi coastal Diveagar beach. The total value of the 107 packets of charas found on different beaches in Raigad district in three days was estimated around Rs 4.50 crore.
Article Summary: The arrested accused was identified as Sadik Abrahim Shekhdare, a resident of Shekhadi village, Shrivardhan taluka. In his police custody remand till July 22, he led the cops to an discarded boat where he had hidden more quantity of charas. The total seized contraband was worth Rs 34.98 lakh.

Article Title: Truck driver arrested from Gujarat for killing fellow driver with iron rod over caste dispute in Maharashtra
Article Text:
Taloja police have caught a truck driver involved in the tragic murder of a fellow driver during a dispute fueled by caste discrimination (Representative image)

NAVI MUMBAI: Taloja police have arrested a 40-year-old truck driver who had absconded after fatally assaulting a 45-year-old truck driver on his head with an iron rod in the truck parking lot of Nisha Transport company in Nitlas village near Taloja industrial area in Panvel taluka on July 14 early morning.The accused was arrested from Valsad railway station, Gujarat on Friday, while he was escaping by train to his home town in UP.The arrested accused has been identified as Ramesh Kumar Yadav and the murder victim as Chandan Pandey, both hailing from UP.Sagar Nikam, PI (crime) of Taloja said, "The murder was an outcome of the Pandey versus Yadav caste discrimination, especially in UP. The accused Yadav had fatally assaulted the victim Pandey as the latter being a Brahmin used to humiliate Yadav from OBC by treating him as inferior, as claimed by the accused Yadav."PI Nikam informed, "On Monday night, an argument has ensued between Pandey and Yadav in the parking lot over caste discrimination. As they quarrelled, the other truck drivers intervened and resolved the matter. On Tuesday around 5.30 am, again both of them quarrelled, when Yadav assaulted on Pandey's head with an iron rod that proved fatal.""Pandey escaped after threatening other truckers if they attempted to catch him. The security guard Mohammad Alam Hajif-ul Khan (58) informed the police. Pandey was rushed to Panvel sub-district hospital where he was declared brought dead. Subsequently, a murder case was registered against the accused Yadav. His photograph found in his parked truck was immediately circulated to the GRP and RPF at railway stations where multiple trains heading to UP halt.""On Friday, the Valsad GRP informed us that Yadav has been detained at Valsad railway station while he was travelling in an express train to escape to his hometown in UP. Our police team reached Valsad and arrested Yadav. The Panvel JMFC court has remanded Yadav to police custody untill July 21."
Article Summary: Ramesh Kumar Yadav, 40, was arrested from Valsad railway station, Gujarat on Friday. He had absconded after fatally assaulting a 45-year-old truck driver on his head with an iron rod. The murder was an outcome of the Pandey versus Yadav caste discrimination, especially in UP.

Article Title: Rag picker's murder detected within 24 hours, accused arrested from Bhiwandi
Article Text:
Rag picker's murder detected within 24 hours, accused arrested from Bhiwandi (Representational Image)

NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai crime branch unit-2 team has arrested a murder accused from Bhiwandi while conducting a parallel probe in the murder case registered at NRI Coastal police station on Friday after an unidentified man's body with head injuries was found on the pavement near D-Mart in sector 15, Belapur on Friday around 1 am.The arrested accused has been identified as Mohammad Irfan Mohammed Husain Ansari (36) and the murder victim as Salman Anwar Shaikh (27), a resident of Govandi. Both working as rag pickers for livelihood.Anil Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-2 informed that, during the probe, when inquired with some rag pickers in the locality, we got an eye witness, who knew Ansari and had seen him assaulting Shaikh with a wooden stick on Thursday night as a quarrel broke out between them after they together consumed liquor near the pavement.The eye witness told that Ansari would pick up rags during day and would spend night where ever he found empty gala or incomplete under construction bldg in Belapur and his father resided in Bhiwandi.Using technical expertise and informer network Ansari was apprehended from Bhiwandi within 24 hours. Thereafter, the murder victim's identity was revealed by him.SPI Patil said, "Ansari claimed that Shaikh was habitual of abusing others after getting drunk. On Thursday night, after the liquor session, Shaikh turned violent without being provoked and attempted to assault him with an iron rod after pushing him to the ground. Hence, he confronted Shaikh by assaulting him with a wooden stick on his head. Seeing Shaikh bleeding profusely and fallen unconscious, he escaped to Bhiwandi. "
Article Summary: Rag picker's murder detected within 24 hours, accused arrested from Bhiwandi. Mohammad Irfan Mohammed Husain Ansari (36) and the murder victim as Salman Anwar Shaikh (27), a resident of Govandi. Both working as rag pickers for livelihood.

Article Title: India will soon bring back World Cup: Ashok Kumar
Article Text:
Ashok Kumar Dhyanchand with Bankers Sports Council officials

Nagpur:





Former Olympian Ashok Kumar Dhyanchand, best known for scoring the winning goal in the 1975 hockey World Cup final, was optimistic of India’s podium finish in Belgium and the Netherlands on Aug 30.Ashok Kumar was in Nagpur to distribute the annual Bankers Sports Council awards on Friday. When asked about India’s chances of winning a second World Cup gold, he said, “Before I speak about India’s chances, the initial thing that comes to my mind is about the first World Cup in 1971, where we won bronze against our target of winning a gold medal. In 1973, we missed the title again despite being 2-0 ahead against Holland in the final. In the extra time, we missed a golden opportunity to win the final and then we missed the penalty stroke, and this setback was painful for all of us.”Two years later in Malaysia, India defeated Pakistan 2-1 to win the 1975 World Cup, where Ashok Kumar scored the match-winner in the 51st minute.He said, “Our final against Pakistan was the best and last example of hockey of that era. Both the teams played top-quality hockey of that time.Then the rules changed, grass became turf and Indian players took time to settle on the artificial surface. In the absence of turf in India, our first camp at Patiala was held on a grass surface spread with cow dung, before we went to play the Montreal Olympics.”India and Argentina played the first match of the Montreal Olympics on artificial turf on July 18, 1976. The shift to synthetic grass severely impacted the traditional playing styles of India and Pakistan. “The turf was imposed on us and Indian hockey was down by four years, Pakistan is still struggling,” he said.Ashok Kumar saw similarities between the 1975 Indian hockey team and the current national contingent, 51 years after the 1975 side’s achievement. He said, “Yesterday, one of my students, whom I taught a little hockey during my coaching period, called me and said, ‘Sir, I am going for the World Cup, tell me something that is beneficial for me and my team.’ Looking at the way he took my suggestion is nothing but an emotion, a feeling that this team wants to win. This team wants to perform that duty which the Indian team of 1975 did, as all the players are supporting each other and are desperate to make their mark. I won’t say we will surely win gold, but we are on the right track to bring the World Cup back sooner and this time we will surely register a podium finish.”When asked about the role of foreign coaches, he said, “When the turf was imposed on us at that time, we needed international coaches. I do not understand why we are spending heavily on foreign coaches. We should spend that amount on preparing turf in tribal areas. Today we have Sardar Singh, Raghunath and many old players who can build a better team. We should hand over some responsibility to them. Hockey India should select 15, 20 players and hand over to the veterans by giving facilities and make them accountable to prepare a medal-winning team. ”
Article Summary: Former Olympian Ashok Kumar Dhyanchand was optimistic of India’s podium finish in Belgium and the Netherlands on Aug 30. He was in Nagpur to distribute the annual Bankers Sports Council awards on Friday. He saw similarities between the 1975 Indian hockey team and the current national contingent.

Article Title: E-challan blunder: Non-functional two-wheeler slapped with 249 wrongful traffic fines to the tune of Rs 3 lakh in Coimbatore
Article Text:
Representative image





COIMBATORE: A non-functional two-wheeler bearing the registration number TN 37 AF 4170 has accumulated 249 pending traffic challans to the tune of more than Rs 3 lakh on the official Parivahan portal.A cross-check of the govt portal revealed a systemic breakdown between 2019 and May 2026. Dozens of traffic violation fines belonging to completely different vehicles were systematically dumped on this single, non-operational bike. The offences, such as riding motorcycles without helmet, rash driving, triple riding, pillion rider without helmet and even drunk driving cases, were transferred to this particular vehicle.The blunder exposes severe flaws in the police's e-challan verification process. In several cases, uploaded evidence photos clearly capture other motorcycles committing offences such as "no parking," yet the fines were slapped on the owners of uninvolved vehicles.B Annammal of Podanur shared her ordeal after receiving a Rs 500 fine. "When I downloaded the challan, my scooter was nowhere in the frame; a completely different bike was parked in the restricted zone," she said."The personnel mistyped my registration number, leaving me penalised for a crime I never committed while the actual violator walked away scot-free."When contacted, Coimbatore city police commissioner N Kannan stated that he was unaware of the issue but promised a thorough inquiry. "We need to determine if this stems from a technical glitch or human error," Kannan said. "If it is a man-made error, we will investigate whether it was done knowingly or unknowingly. Severe action will be taken if any malpractices are uncovered."S S Maheswaran, deputy commissioner of police (traffic), Coimbatore city, stated that they would verify with the technical team and try to resolve the issue.
Article Summary: A non-functional two-wheeler bearing the registration number TN 37 AF 4170 has accumulated 249 pending traffic challans. The offences, such as riding motorcycles without helmet, rash driving, triple riding, pillion rider without helmet and even drunk driving cases, were transferred to this particular vehicle. The blunder exposes severe flaws in the police's e-challan verification process.

Article Title: Illegal garbage dumping: Coimbatore corporation collects Rs 4 lakh fine from four offenders
Article Text:
Representative image





COIMBATORE: The Coimbatore corporation has intensified crackdown on illegal garbage dumping, imposing a total fine of Rs 4 lakh on four offenders during surprise inspections across the city.During the inspection on Wednesday, corporation officials found several instances of garbage illegally dumped in public places. Acting on the directions of corporation commissioner Katta Ravi Teja, officials imposed a fine of Rs 1 lakh each on four individuals responsible for creating large garbage dumps instead of ensuring proper disposal. A total of Rs 4 lakh was imposed.In a separate case, a person who had dumped waste near the corporation electric crematorium at Veerakeralam in Ward 40 was identified with police assistance. The corporation’s health team imposed a fine of Rs 20,000 and warned the person against dumping waste in public places and waterbodies.According to corporation officials, around 1,215 metric tonne (MT) of solid waste is collected daily from households and commercial establishments in 100 wards. Of this, about 835 MT comprises biodegradable waste and 380 MT consists of non-biodegradable waste, which are segregated and processed at composting centres.According to a release form corporation, it is closely monitoring efforts to achieve 100% door-to-door waste collection, with sanitation workers, vehicle drivers and sanitary supervisors deployed across all wards. It is conducting awareness campaigns through pamphlets, rallies, banners, loudspeaker announcements and wall murals to educate residents on the four categories of waste segregation prescribed under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026—biodegradable waste, non-biodegradable waste, sanitary waste and special waste. Weekly review meetings are being held in all five corporation zones to monitor solid waste management activities.
Article Summary: The Coimbatore corporation has intensified crackdown on illegal garbage dumping. Officials imposed a total fine of Rs 4 lakh on four offenders during surprise inspections across the city. Around 1,215 metric tonne of solid waste is collected daily from households and commercial establishments in 100 wards.
